title: Dependency injection: providers, tokens and hierarchical injectors

videos.script:
The week screen reads today from the computer's clock. Nobody can hand it a different day, so nobody can test it on one. This lesson fixes that, and on the way it shows the idea the whole of Angular stands on.

{{asking}} A class says what it needs, and an injector hands it over. You ask for a greeter that nobody provides, and Angular refuses with en-gee zero two oh one. One argument, provided-in root, and the greeter arrives.

{{providers}} Then the four recipes an injector can follow: a class, a value, a factory, or another token. You swap one class for another without touching the component that asks.

{{tokens}} Today is not a class, so it gets a token of its own. The week asks for it, and a test names its own day.

{{hierarchy}} Injectors form a tree. Where a recipe sits decides who shares what it makes, and two counters show both answers.

{{context}} And inject works only while something is being built. Call it from a click, and you meet the error that says so.
